name: Zendesk
description: Read-only Zendesk Support access: tickets, users and cross-object search on one tenant instance

tools.name: list_tickets
tools.description: List Zendesk support tickets, most recently requested first

tools.name: get_ticket
tools.description: Get one Zendesk ticket by its numeric ID

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: List Zendesk users (agents and end users), optionally filtered by role

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search Zendesk across tickets, users and organizations with the Zendesk search syntax (e.g. 'type:ticket status:open')

needs_review: AUTH SHAPE NOW MATCHES THE LIVE-TESTED REGISTRY FORM, BUT HAS NOT BEEN RUN AGAINST A REAL INSTANCE. Spec v1.1 gained auth.userSuffix on basic auth, so this spec sends Basic base64("{{email}}/token:{{api_token}}"), the same bytes as services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js key 'zendesk', which is Zendesk's documented API-token form. What is proven: the runtime assembles that username (services/collector/test/connectorDeclarativeRuntime.test.js, 'basic auth userSuffix'), and the shape-proof below proves host, TLS, base_url template rendering and every path, because Zendesk answers a rejected credential with a structured 401 at the real paths and a 404 InvalidEndpoint at a bogus one. What is NOT proven: no Zendesk credential was held, so a 2xx has never been observed on this connector.

base_url is now the Spec v1.1 template form "https://{{subdomain}}.zendesk.com", matching the registry's testEndpoint; the scaffolded fromCredential key was dropped because the credential holds a bare subdomain slug, not a host. base_url._probe substitutes the public subdomain "support" (Zendesk's own support.zendesk.com instance) so the blind harness has a host that resolves. The probe value is read-only, used with a dummy credential, and the runtime ignores _probe entirely.
Category set to 'communication' to match the shipped taxonomy used by the other support desks (front, crisp); the scaffolded 'uncategorized' is not a real bucket.

Payload field names come from the Zendesk developer documentation (tools_source), not from a live 2xx: no Zendesk instance was held for this draft, so response picks are documentary. get_ticket declares ticket_id as a number because Zendesk ticket IDs are numeric.
